source.title: The Hidden Dimensions of LLM Alignment: A Multi-Dimensional Analysis of Orthogonal Safety Directions
source.authors: Wenbo Pan; Zhi-Chao Liu; Qi-Guang Chen; Xiangyang Zhou; Haining Yu; Xiao-Hua Jia

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study intervenes on a dominant residual-space direction and on non-dominant directions, and reports refusal outcomes. Its results refine the single-direction account by describing a dominant direction together with additional behaviorally relevant directions.
record.gate_note: The paper studies directions from activation shifts during SSFT or DPO, not the original harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. It reports a one-layer dominant-direction intervention and interventions on other directions, but does not add a direction. Values used only to choose components or settings are not recorded as results. Cited findings from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study removes a dominant fine-tuning-shift direction (L25-C1), which eliminates refusal. It also removes non-dominant directions with selective effects (L14-C6 on PAIR prompts; suppression cuts jailbreak refusal from 96.7% to 14.4%). The authors argue refusal is a dominant direction plus secondary directions, which restates V1 as V4. The directions are SVD components of the activation shift from safety fine-tuning, not harmful-minus-harmless mean differences, and the subject is the authors' own safety-fine-tuned Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the authors attribute the multiple directions to safety fine-tuning learning spurious correlations with jailbreak patterns. They show that a trigger-removal attack exploiting this resists further safety fine-tuning, keeping about 40% success after 80-shot exposure.
record.recipe_differences: The study fits an affine map to activation changes during safety fine-tuning and takes SVD components of the resulting residual space. It intervenes on selected components at specified layers rather than deriving a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction and projecting it out everywhere.
record.method_sensitivity: The residual-space rank and behavior depend on training approach (SSFT versus DPO); trigger-removal attack scores also vary with exposure examples and fine-tuning setup.

fits_no_version.finding: The effective rank of the safety fine-tuning activation shift is 1 in SSFT early layers and peaks near layer 20. At the final layer it falls to 1 for SSFT but keeps rising for DPO.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The dimensionality of fine-tuning-induced safety representation shifts depends on the training objective (SSFT vs DPO).

fits_no_version.finding: The trigger-removal jailbreak keeps about 40% attack pass rate after 80-shot adversarial fine-tuning, while other jailbreaks fall to near zero. Strong Reject Scores fall with exposure under SSFT, DPO, and SFT+DPO.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreaks crafted to avoid tokens tied to the dominant safety direction resist adversarial safety fine-tuning.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR 267, 2025)
record.problems: The main causal refusal intervention is reported for a selected direction at one layer, not for projection at every layer and position. Most intervention effects are described qualitatively or shown in figures without exact values. The general-capability check is Alpaca perplexity rather than a broad capability evaluation, and no statistical uncertainty is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted detailed outcomes for other jailbreak methods and OR-Bench from Tables 3 and 5-7 because they do not measure the Trigger Removal Attack or the direction-specific claim. Omitted model-scale/architecture jailbreak performance plots in Appendix C.3 because they do not report transfer of the direction itself.

untested.parts: Difference-in-means construction; adding the direction to induce refusal; all-layer, all-position ablation; broad capability benchmarks (only Alpaca perplexity).
Training against the direction's ablation (training only adds attack examples).
Transfer across languages, variants, or base to instruct.
No test of whether the training method changes removability of a single direction; DPO has no removal experiment.

missing.what: Best-of-N SSFT components have near-zero cosine with the Arditi-style probe vector yet nearly match its refusal-prediction accuracy; the probe vector beats the dominant direction in early layers. Bears on V4 (the probe aggregates multiple directions).
Removing L14-C4 and L14-C3 also changes refusal, without clear selectivity across attacks.
PLRP relevance of layer-14 components to L25-C1: C1 0.517, C2 -0.108, C5 0.094, C6 0.086. Secondary directions promote or suppress the dominant one.
Replication on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct with DPO: effective rank and dominant-direction prediction accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche T5: the study refines the single-direction account into a dominant direction plus secondary directions. The subject throughout is the authors' own safety-fine-tuned Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; directions come from SVD of the fitted affine fine-tuning shift at the first generated token. The non-dominance suppression removes all 4096 directions before layer 10, including the dominant one there, so it is not purely non-dominant. No uncertainty is reported. Most intervention effects (Figure 4, Figure 6) are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: The direction is not constructed as the original harmful-minus-harmless difference in means. The paper tests removal at a specified layer, not projection from every layer and position; it does not test adding the direction or measure a broad suite of other abilities.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration procedure is tested.

The attack is trigger-token removal/rephrasing, not a direct intervention that suppresses the direction. Training uses examples of the trigger-removal attack; the paper does not train against an ablation of the direction.
The paper does not test an affine refusal set or concept cone.
No separate harmfulness-judgment versus refusal-decision representation is tested.
No cross-language direction transfer or transfer of a direction between base and instruct models is tested.
The paper compares SSFT and DPO residual-space properties, but does not establish how different training schedules or stages determine whether a removable single direction exists across models.

source_check.notes: Appendix C.1/C.2 say SSFT trained the model to output safe/unsafe classification labels (Llama Guard style), while Sec. 3.2 says it trained refusals; 'refusal' in SSFT results may mean outputting the 'unsafe' label. statements.correction: 2502.09674: Trigger Removal Attack (authors' own) applies token-wise PLRP to final-layer dominant directions to find trigger tokens, then rephrases prompts to avoid them (Sec. 6, App. B). On the authors' SSFT Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct it shifts dominant-component (LN-C1, SVD of fine-tuning shift, not DiM) projections closer to benign samples, with lower refusal; figure-only (Fig. 6). Drop r37 from this line or list it as a direction-targeted attack.
statements.problem: This study is cited (r37) as support for 'ordinary attacks, not built to target the direction'. Its Trigger Removal Attack is built from the dominant direction itself. The conditions line ('2–14B instruct or chat models') also omits that the model was safety-fine-tuned by the authors.

statements.correction: r3 SSFT and r4 DPO: the dominant direction predicts refusal with high accuracy in later layers (Fig. 3, no number). r5: removing L14-C6 removes refusal to PAIR prompts only. r6/r7 (SSFT): suppression covers all 4096 directions before layer 10; after layer 15, about 2 directions per layer with harmfulness correlation >0.7 are kept. Jailbreak refusal 96.7%→14.4%, StrongReject harmful 100%→80%, benign 10%→0% (Table 8). ICML 2025, code y, Alpaca perplexity check y; authors Pan et al.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but r4 is DPO, not SSFT. The conditions line says 'L14 in 2502.09674', which fits only r5. The non-dominant suppression in r6/r7 spans all layers, and r3/r4 concern later layers.
Minor: the 'non-dominant' suppression also removes all directions before layer 10, dominant ones included (App. D).
